chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalat ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
The one performing Itikaaf in Makkah prays in whichever of its houses he desires; it is the same to him whether he prays in the Masjid or in its houses.

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: The Masjid (specifically Masjid al-Haram in this context)
key_terms.بُيُوتِهَا: Its houses (adjacent structures to the Masjid)

ai.seo_question: Where can a person perform Itikaaf prayers in Makkah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the flexibility of Itikaaf in Makkah, distinguishing it from the stricter requirement of remaining within the Masjid boundaries in other locations. It reflects the scholarly view that the sanctity of Makkah allows the 'houses' (bayt) to serve as valid extensions of the sacred precinct for spiritual retreat. This ruling underscores the practical ease granted to pilgrims while maintaining the spiritual integrity of the retreat.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
‘The one performing Itikaaf in Makkah can Pray in whichever of its house he so desires to. It is the same to him whether he Prays in the Masjid or he Prays in its houses’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One performing ’Ttikaf in Makkah can perform Salat (prayer) in any of its houses or Masjid; it is all the same.’”
